newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Prescott sees no new ministries.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Prescott sees no new ministries.

text.p: John Prescott, deputy leader of Britain's Labour party, said he did not expect new government departments to be established in economic policy.

Asked in a BBC radio interview asked about speculation that he might head a new "super-department of economic affairs" or if other new departments might be created, he replied: "No, there won't be new departments."
But powerful economic bodies and agencies would implement Labour policies.

Prescott, likely to be deputy prime minister under Tony Blair, dismissed calls by Labour left-winger Ken Livingstone for substantial tax increases and said Labour would implement the programme on which it had been elected.

"I only want to perhaps suggest that to depart from that would be not the best way to keep the trust of people, not only now but certainly at the second election, when we wish to return and ask for another five years," he said.
